key_insight: Genetic liability to adult internalizing–cardiometabolic multimorbidity is associated with early-life mental and cardiometabolic changes and higher levels of inflammatory proteins.
clinical_relevance: These findings highlight potential early biological pathways linking mental and cardiometabolic conditions, but do not establish clinical screening or treatment strategies.
method: Studied 5,934 participants in the UK ALSPAC birth cohort.
Used mixed-effects models to assess associations between polygenic liability and trajectories of 12 health outcomes.
Examined circulating inflammatory proteins at ages 9 and 24 using the Olink Target 96 Inflammation panel.
evidence_signal: Higher polygenic liability was consistently associated with higher IL6, TNFSF14 and HGF levels at both ages 9 and 24.
watch_item: Observational associations in one UK cohort do not establish causality or generalizability; this is not an AI cancer drug discovery study.
paper_title: Early-life hallmarks of polygenic liability to adult internalizing-cardiometabolic multimorbidity
